title: Tarzan
paragraphs: Original American Gold Seal transcribed Tarzan serial distributed station-by-station. Historical run totals 286 installments; the frozen GRH snapshot contains surviving installments 1-77 with Los Angeles weekday-reference dates from September 12 through December 27, 1932.
GRH documents the program through Tarzan of the Apes adaptation (September 12, 1932 to March 10, 1933) and The Return of Tarzan continuation (March 13, 1933 to March 9, 1934).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include survival and physical peril, rescue, capture and escape, ships, sailors, mutiny and shipwreck, wildlife danger and animal encounters, jungle wilderness, and apes and jungle animal society.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Early transcription-disc syndication, Signal Oil sponsorship and radio merchandising, and Print adventure franchise moves to radio.
plain_text:
Original American Gold Seal transcribed Tarzan serial distributed station-by-station. Historical run totals 286 installments; the frozen GRH snapshot contains surviving installments 1-77 with Los Angeles weekday-reference dates from September 12 through December 27, 1932.

GRH documents the program through Tarzan of the Apes adaptation (September 12, 1932 to March 10, 1933) and The Return of Tarzan continuation (March 13, 1933 to March 9, 1934).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include survival and physical peril, rescue, capture and escape, ships, sailors, mutiny and shipwreck, wildlife danger and animal encounters, jungle wilderness, and apes and jungle animal society.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Early transcription-disc syndication, Signal Oil sponsorship and radio merchandising, and Print adventure franchise moves to radio.
